item.text:
Refactored [BinarySearchTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/013_binary_search_tree_searching/BinarySearchTree.java) into a more coherent collection-style API. The main design change is that insertion is now explicit about duplicate handling: `add(...)` returns `true` only when a new value is inserted, `addAll(...)` reports how many values were actually added, and the tree tracks `size` directly. That makes the behavior around duplicates visible instead of implicit.

I also made the tree implement `Iterable<T>` with an in-order iterator, which gives it a cleaner reusable interface for traversal instead of treating it as a search-only container. The natural-order constructor path was tightened through `create()` and shared null validation is centralized.

[BinarySearchTreeSearching.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/013_binary_search_tree_searching/BinarySearchTreeSearching.java) did not need behavioral changes. Verification: `javac BinarySearchTree.java BinarySearchTreeSearching.java` succeeded, and `java BinarySearchTreeSearching` still prints `true`.
